A galvanometer having a coil resistance
100 <mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="SVG" overflow="overflow"><svg style="vertical-align: 0;" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="1.633ex" height="1.593ex" role="img" focusable="false" viewBox="0 -704 722 704" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><g stroke="currentColor" fill="currentColor" stroke-width="0" transform="scale(1,-1)"><g data-mml-node="math"><g data-mml-node="mi"><use data-c="3A9" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-N-3A9"></use></g></g></g></svg></mjx-container> gives a full scale deflection when a
current of 1 mA is passed through it. What is
the value of the resistance which can convert
this galvanometer into a voltmeter giving full
scale deflection for a potential difference of
10 V?

7.9 k<mjx-container class="MathJax" jax="SVG" overflow="overflow"><svg style="vertical-align: 0;" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="1.633ex" height="1.593ex" role="img" focusable="false" viewBox="0 -704 722 704" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><g stroke="currentColor" fill="currentColor" stroke-width="0" transform="scale(1,-1)"><g data-mml-node="math"><g data-mml-node="mi"><use data-c="3A9" xlink:href="#MJX-TEX-N-3A9"></use></g></g></g></svg></mjx-container>

explanation:
ig = 1 mA , Rg = 100

V = ig(R + Rg)

10 = 1 × 10–3 (R + 100)

R = 9.9 k
